issues.finding: The length definition omits falsity; disjunction cut rank refers to undefined A/B instead of A1/A2; the displayed maximum omits the stipulated zero for normal terms.
issues.proposed_resolution: Define falsity length as zero, use A1/A2 for the sum cut rank, and include zero in the maximum.

issues.finding: The disjunction-elimination major term is printed as i rather than the substituted variable x.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use x as the major term in the disjunction-elimination case.

issues.location: substitution lemma rank and projection case
issues.finding: A stray parenthesis occurs in the rank equality; the proof then refers to cutrank(x), which is undefined for a variable.
issues.proposed_resolution: Remove the stray parenthesis and identify the rank with the length of the variable's type.

issues.finding: The beta and sum cases omit redexes copied from the substituting argument.
issues.proposed_resolution: Add the inherited-argument cases; their smaller rank follows directly from the proper-subterm hypothesis.

issues.location: normalization theorem contextual and permutation proof gap
issues.finding: The lemma bounds redexes inside the reductum, not newly exposed redexes in enclosing eliminations. A sum elimination can return a product or arrow of greater length. Permutation redexes also have no rank in the definitions. Thus the asserted whole-term rank decrease does not follow.
issues.proposed_resolution: Preserve the translated source argument with an adjacent Javanese editorial footnote explicitly identifying the missing contextual and permutation control. Keep proof repair open.

issues.finding: The first projection of the pair with updated first component is erroneously said to reduce to O2. The text also says subterm redexes cannot overlap, although nesting is possible.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use O1-prime as the common reduct, qualify overlap as partial overlap, and state the discarded-component case.

issues.finding: The proof sketches disjoint reductions and one nested projection example but does not establish the remaining nested contractions or permutation interactions used by the full preceding calculus.
issues.proposed_resolution: Add an adjacent Javanese editorial footnote identifying the proof as a sketch and leave the remaining cases open.

issues.finding: Both sequences define N1 as the original N, while the subsequent argument requires N1 to be the first successor.
issues.proposed_resolution: Start both displayed sequences at N0 and show the first step to N1.

issues.finding: Weak Church-Rosser supplies a common reduct, which need not itself be normal; the proof compares it with the two chosen normal forms as though it were.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use strong normalization to normalize the common reduct and designate that common normal form N-triple-prime before comparing normal forms.

issues.location: normalization theorem scope and its introductory/proof prose
issues.finding: The following proof-terms section explicitly distinguishes arbitrary syntactic proof terms from correct, well-typed proof terms. The unrestricted normalization statement would include nonnormalizing self-application terms.
issues.proposed_resolution: Qualify the theorem, introduction and induction domain to well-typed proof terms; retain the disclosed proof gaps.
